subject: Political Science
central_question: Why did the Soviet-led bipolar order collapse, and how did its end reshape post-communist societies, world politics and India’s relations with Russia?
in_scope_units: Overview: the Berlin Wall, the end of the Cold War and the collapse of the second world
What was the Soviet System: socialism, state planning, welfare, one-party rule and the socialist bloc
Gorbachev and the Disintegration: reforms, East European protests, the 1991 coup and the dissolution of the USSR
Why did the Soviet Union Disintegrate: economic stagnation, political rigidity, public alienation and nationalism
Consequences of Disintegration: end of the Cold War, unipolarity, capitalism, liberal democracy and new states
Shock Therapy in Post-Communist Regimes: rapid transition from socialism to capitalism
Consequences of Shock Therapy: industrial collapse, inflation, poverty, inequality and weak democratic institutions
Tensions and Conflicts: secessionism, civil wars, ethnic conflict and outside-power competition
India and Post-communist Countries: India–Russia relations, multipolarity, defence, energy, science and culture
banned_topics: Detailed origins and phases of the Cold War before the Soviet collapse
A full account of United States hegemony after 1991
Detailed domestic politics of independent India unrelated to India–USSR or India–Russia relations

known_pitfalls.claim: The Soviet Union collapsed only because Gorbachev introduced reforms.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter identifies deeper economic stagnation, political rigidity, public alienation and nationalism; Gorbachev’s reforms accelerated forces already present.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Soviet system had no achievements.
known_pitfalls.correction: It became a great power, built major industrial and infrastructural capacity, and provided subsidised welfare and a minimum standard of living.
It also involved free trade, FDI, deregulation, currency convertibility, private farming and a reorientation towards the Western economic system.

known_pitfalls.claim: The USSR’s collapse ended India’s close relationship with Russia.
known_pitfalls.correction: India retained strong relations with Russia in defence, energy, nuclear, space, science and diplomacy.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 6 to compare the Soviet economy with a capitalist economy.
Use NCERT Exercise 7 to organise the economic and political pressures behind Gorbachev’s reforms.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to connect Soviet disintegration with changes faced by India.
Use NCERT Exercise 9 to evaluate shock therapy using evidence from its consequences.
Use NCERT Exercise 10 to construct a balanced argument about India’s relations with the US and Russia.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The NCERT end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–10, including objective, chronological, matching, short-answer and essay questions.
